rv.q: I am so glad I stayed in my seat for this lovely, lovely show.
The cast are utterly stellar, and every single actor stands out.

The Royal Shakespeare Company’s production is a soulful, colourful, and uplifting example of how musical adaptation can bring a story to new heights, layering in a new dimension for a pre-existing tale.
The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind is incredibly rich and uplifting.

Guided by scraps of knowledge and a sympathetic librarian, he begins to imagine a windmill that could generate electricity and save his community from famine. It is a compelling premise, and Richy Hughes’ book and lyrics ensure that the stakes are always clear.

In many ways, @sohoplace is the perfect venue for The Boy The Wind: the intimate thrust staging is perfect for elaborate ensemble choreography and carousing the audience. This new musical, based on the memoir and film of the same name, is at its heart a story about community, and it works if we feel as immersed in that community as possible.
But if you dislike folksy theatre, this may not suit you.

cn.t: Critics praise this inspiring RSC musical for its vibrant storytelling and powerful ensemble work, celebrating William Kamkwamba's remarkable true story with moving performances and joyous energy in the intimate @sohoplace venue.

dr.inst: Released via TodayTix app only at 10 AM.
